newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firms up at close on strong GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firms up at close on strong GDP data.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended earlier strength to close firmer across the board on Thursday, boosted by third quarter GDP data released during the session, traders said.
"The peso traded strongly due to local dealers dumping dollar positions and real year-on-year Q3 growth," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed closed 1.5 and 2.5 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8750/7.8790 and 7.8590/7.8630 per dollar.
The same-day peso had earlier closed 0.8 of a centavo firmer at 7.8740/7.8770 per dollar.
The third quarter grew 7.4 percent, the second consecutive quarter to have posted a year-on-year increase since the recession spurred by the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
The good news from GDP brightened a dark mood at the start of the day on a lower-than-expected preliminary trade surplus of $277 million for October that were realeased on Wednesday night.
"The trade balance was not good, but solid GDP data was uppermost in dealers' minds and improved market feeling and bolstered the peso," said another trader.

The market was indifferent to Friday's maturity of a $1.5 billion sovereign dual currency bond issued one year ago, which will pay the highest rate of either 12-month Libor or 28-day Cetes less 600 basis points.
"There must be some foreseen way to cover the maturity, otherwise the market would not be so stable," said a trader.
Traders said the peso could extend ground gained on Friday, but saw pressure from traditional month-end demand for dollars beginning next week.
"We feel the 48-hour rate could reach 7.87 per dollar tomorrow and then return to around 7.94 next week as the month draws to a close," a trader said.
